passages.original: δὲ ὡς τόπος φωνῆς, ὅταν λέγωμεν δώριον ἤ φρύγιον ἢ λύδιον ἢ τῶν ἄλλων τινά. εἰσὶ δὲ κατὰ Ἀριστόξενον ιγ τόνοι.
passages.english: …and as a region of the voice, when we speak of the Dorian or Phrygian or Lydian or any of the others. According to Aristoxenus there are thirteen tonoi [keys].
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence with δὲ, picking up an enumeration of the senses of τόνος ("tone"). The earlier senses fall outside the passage. Here τόνος is used in the sense of "key" or "pitch-region" (τόπος φωνῆς). ιγ is the Greek numeral 13.
